newsitem.title: USA: FEATURE-Clinton guru Dick Morris searches for respect.
newsitem.headline: FEATURE-Clinton guru Dick Morris searches for respect.

text.p: As President Bill Clinton begins his second term, the political guru who helped him pull off his re-election miracle wanders the New York and Washington talk show circuit searching for respect.
But like a beggar at a banquet Dick Morris is getting only crumbs -- being caught in a toe-sucking sex scandal takes its toll on a person's reputation, as Fergie, the Duchess of York, can attest.

When Morris shows up before the cameras to talk about his new book, "Behind the Oval Office: Winning the Presidency in the Nineties," the first few questions are about politics and the rest about his cavorting with a prostitute in Washington. The woman, apparently bored with his prancing about on all fours and telling her administration secrets, blew the whistle to a supermarket tabloid.
One of her complaints was that she thought the country should be run by adults.

"What do you think about now when you see an ad for an escort service?" one TV interviewer asked recently as she pumped Morris full of questions about why he let the prostitute listen in on his conversations with the president.

Morris responds indirectly. "I have gone 146 days without (illicit sex). I hope to wake up tomorrow and say 147 days," he said. "I was using sex as a solution when horniness wasn't the problem," he added.
FORGET THE SEX, REVIEWERS SAY

But as a few reviewers are pointing out, the interviewers should forget about sex and read Morris's book for what it reveals about the American politcal process. Therein may lie the real scandal -- a scandal about how politicians tailor their messages to say exactly what the public wants to hear.

Morris, a one-time liberal who swung right years ago, was called in by his old friend Clinton in 1994 after Republicans had won both houses of Congress for the first time in 40 years and the polls said the president was not just a lame duck but a dead duck when it came to a hoped-for second term.
Within two years, Morris made Clinton unbeatable, and in his book he is very frank about how he did it.

For starters, he took poll after poll to find out what the public wanted. He says the polls showed the public was tired of negative politics, so he turned Clinton positive -- pumping for smaller government while at the same time pressing for politically popular programmes, often just little things that change the quality of life, like the family leave act.
He turned Clinton into a neo-Republican, a man capable of taking Republican positions on many key issues but reshaping or rephrasing them as if they were his own.
Morris told Reuters recently while Clinton would not use polls to find a political position he would use a poll to find out how to fine-tune what he believes.

For example, Clinton is opposed to a constitutional amendment that would allow school prayer. "So we did some polls to find out what the public wants to happen in schools. They want ethics taught. They want young people taught abstinence. They want a want a moment of silence, and we can do all that without a constitutional amendment."
"DE-FANGING THE ISSUE"
The Republicans wanted an across-the-boards tax cut. Clinton-Morris responded with targeted tax cuts. "It's called de-fanging the issue," Morris said.

Others complain that is not the way to run a presidency. The president should lead, they say. The president should use the White House as a "bully pulpit," a phrase the public likes so much it has shown up in administration pronouncements.

Morris took polls on everything, even where Clinton should go on vacation. Americans think golf, which Clinton loves, is for rich people. So Morris polled and told Clinton to go hiking. The president did, with his family in tow.

On and on it went. Clinton did not want to justify an invasion of Haiti by saying that was the only way to keep tens of thousands of Haitian refugees from engulfing Florida and becoming a political liabilty. So Morris suggested he stress "the human rights and values" issues to sell an invasion.

Now Morris is out of the loop, as they say in Washington. He will not say whether he and the president are still talking because "we've agreed I won't say anything until he's out of office, whether we talk or don't talk."
